concept.name: Materialized View Refresh Strategies

relationships.description: Connects Materialized View Refresh Strategies to database indexing in the broader engineering catalog.

spark.summary: Materialized view refresh precomputes and updates expensive joins or aggregations on disk so analytical queries read in milliseconds, trading bounded staleness and write/refresh overhead for read speed.
spark.keyTakeaway: Choose full concurrent refresh for simple batch dashboards, and incremental or CDC-driven refresh when tables exceed tens of millions of rows or require sub-minute freshness.

concept.whyItMatters: Joining 500M-row fact tables with dimension tables on every dashboard load burns CPU, saturates I/O, and blows past 200 ms API budgets. Materialized views (MVs) turn O(N) runtime scans into O(1) or O(K) indexed lookups—provided the refresh strategy does not lock out readers or fall behind write throughput.
whenToUse: Read-heavy dashboards, leaderboards, and APIs executing repeated multi-table `JOIN` + `GROUP BY` aggregations over millions of rows.
Systems that can tolerate bounded staleness (e.g., 5 seconds to 1 hour) in exchange for predictable < 20 ms read latency.
OLAP/HTAP engines (ClickHouse `AggregatingMergeTree`, Snowflake Dynamic Tables, Postgres MVs) where pre-aggregation cuts compute cost by 10x–100x.
whenNotToUse: Strict read-your-own-writes transactional paths (e.g., checking live bank balance before a transfer).
High-cardinality ad-hoc filtering where users slice by arbitrary unindexed columns—querying the MV becomes as slow as the base table.
Write-saturated base tables when using non-incremental full refreshes that thrash disk I/O and autovacuum.
keyPoints: Full refresh (`REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW`) recomputes the entire query from scratch and acquires an `AccessExclusiveLock` in PostgreSQL, blocking all `SELECT`s unless `CONCURRENTLY` is used.
`REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY` in PostgreSQL requires at least one `UNIQUE` index on the MV and performs a diff-merge, allowing reads during refresh at ~2x–3x slower refresh time.
Incremental View Maintenance (IVM) / CDC-based MVs (ClickHouse, Oracle `FAST REFRESH`, pg_ivm, Flink/Debezium) apply only row deltas (`INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE`) in O(Δ) time.
Non-monotonic operations (`DISTINCT`, `MEDIAN`, `PERCENTILE_CONT`, `NOT EXISTS`, outer joins) are hard or impossible to maintain incrementally without auxiliary state.
Staleness SLAs must be monitored explicitly via `last_refreshed_at` or `TARGET_LAG` metrics rather than assuming cron jobs always finish on time.

examples.title: PostgreSQL Concurrent Refresh for SaaS Billing Dashboard
examples.scenario: A 120M-row `usage_events` table took 14 seconds per tenant aggregation query, timing out the customer portal.
examples.outcome: Creating a daily-rollup MV with a `UNIQUE (tenant_id, day)` index and scheduling `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY` every 15 minutes dropped portal p99 from 14 s to 11 ms with zero read locks.

examples.title: ClickHouse Incremental MV for Real-Time Ad Impressions
examples.scenario: Ingesting 250,000 events/sec made periodic full SQL refreshes impossible within a 30-second freshness SLA.
examples.outcome: An `AggregatingMergeTree` target table fed by a ClickHouse `MATERIALIZED VIEW` using `-State`/`-Merge` combinators updated hourly rollups at ingest time with < 2 s lag.

tradeOffs.factor: Full Refresh vs. Incremental / Delta Refresh
tradeOffs.pro: Full refresh is trivial to author in SQL and supports arbitrary window functions and `PERCENTILE` logic.
tradeOffs.con: Compute cost scales with total table size O(N) on every tick, eventually exceeding the refresh interval.
Requires a unique index, uses extra temp/WAL space for the diff, and runs 2x–3x slower than an exclusive swap.

tradeOffs.factor: Eager (On-Commit) IVM vs. Scheduled / Lag-Based Refresh
tradeOffs.pro: On-commit triggers/IVM keep the view strictly fresh with zero staleness.
tradeOffs.con: Adds write amplification and lock contention to every OLTP `INSERT`/`UPDATE` transaction.

failureModes.name: AccessExclusiveLock Read Outage
failureModes.description: Running `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW` without `CONCURRENTLY` in PostgreSQL blocks all dashboard `SELECT` queries for minutes, piling up API threads.
failureModes.mitigation: Always add a `UNIQUE` index and use `CONCURRENTLY`, or build a new table and atomically `ALTER TABLE ... RENAME`.

failureModes.name: Refresh Overlap & Queue Spiral
failureModes.description: Data grows so a 5-minute cron refresh takes 7 minutes; overlapping jobs contend on locks and exhaust DB CPU.
failureModes.mitigation: Acquire a non-blocking advisory lock (`pg_try_advisory_lock`) at job start so overlapping runs skip cleanly, and alert when duration > 70% of interval.

failureModes.name: MV Log / WAL Bloat
failureModes.description: If an incremental refresh consumer stalls, materialized view change logs (`MLOG$_*`) or replication slots grow unboundedly until disk fills.
failureModes.mitigation: Monitor replication lag and log table size; set alert thresholds and fallback to full snapshot re-sync if lag exceeds retention.

failureModes.name: Silent Staleness After Failed Job
failureModes.description: A refresh fails due to a schema change or timeout, leaving dashboards serving 3-day-old numbers with no user warning.
failureModes.mitigation: Store `refreshed_at` metadata in the view or control table and surface freshness badges + PagerDuty alerts on SLA breach.

commonMistakes: Forgetting to create indexes on the materialized view itself (it starts with zero indexes beyond any required unique index).
Using `REFRESH ... CONCURRENTLY` on an empty or newly created MV before an initial non-concurrent populate.
Writing `SELECT *` in an MV without explicit column types, causing refreshes to break on upstream `ALTER TABLE`.
Expecting ClickHouse `MATERIALIZED VIEW` to retroactively update when `UPDATE`/`DELETE` mutations hit the source table (it only triggers on `INSERT` blocks).
Storing non-additive metrics like `AVG()` directly in incremental rollups instead of storing `SUM` + `COUNT` (or `-State` combinators).

sections.content:
## The idea

A regular SQL view is a saved query macro—every `SELECT` re-executes the underlying joins and scans. A **materialized view (MV)** persists the query result physically on disk (and buffer pool/page cache), turning expensive `O(N)` scans into fast `O(log N)` or `O(1)` indexed reads.

The core engineering problem is **maintenance**: how to keep the materialized copy synchronized with mutating base tables without blocking readers or amplifying write latency beyond budget. Strategies span a spectrum from **periodic full recomputation** (`O(N)`), to **concurrent diff-swaps**, to **incremental delta maintenance** (`O(Δ)` via CDC or engine-native triggers).

## Concrete walkthrough

Walk through PostgreSQL `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY` on a 50M-row `orders` table summarized into `daily_revenue_mv` (50k rows):

1. **Unique Key Requirement**: Create `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_rev_pk ON daily_revenue_mv (merchant_id, order_date)` so Postgres can uniquely identify rows during diffing.
2. **Snapshot Execution**: When `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY daily_revenue_mv` runs, Postgres executes the view query against a consistent MVCC snapshot into a temporary internal table.
3. **Full Outer Diff**: Postgres performs a full outer join between the old MV and the temp table on `(merchant_id, order_date)` to find only inserted, updated, or deleted rows (say 1,200 changed rows).
4. **Non-Blocking Apply**: Only those 1,200 rows are inserted/updated/deleted in `daily_revenue_mv` under a `RowExclusiveLock`, allowing concurrent `SELECT` queries to read clean snapshots with zero downtime.

nodes.sublabel: Temp snapshot diff or CDC delta agg

edges.label: WAL deltas or snapshot
edges.title: Capture source changes
edges.description: Either stream row-level CDC deltas from the WAL or read a consistent MVCC snapshot of base tables.

edges.label: Aggregate & diff
edges.title: Compute changed rollup keys
edges.description: Aggregate partial states (SUM/COUNT) or diff the new snapshot against the current MV via its unique index.

edges.label: Apply minimal delta
edges.title: Upsert changed rows non-blockingly
edges.description: Write only modified rows into the MV under row-level locks, keeping concurrent reads unblocked.

edges.label: Indexed SELECT
edges.title: Serve low-latency analytical reads
edges.description: API queries hit pre-aggregated rows via B-tree or MergeTree primary keys in milliseconds.

edges.label: Rows + refreshed_at
edges.title: Return results with freshness metadata
edges.description: Response includes last_refreshed_at so clients and monitors can verify staleness SLA compliance.

data.caption: Whether using PostgreSQL concurrent diff-refresh or CDC/ClickHouse incremental aggregation, isolating delta computation keeps analytical reads fast and lock-free.

sections.content:
## Incremental algebra & algebraic aggregates

Not all SQL expressions can be maintained incrementally in `O(Δ)` time:

- **Distributive / Algebraic Aggregates (`COUNT`, `SUM`, `MIN`, `MAX`, `AVG`)**: `SUM` and `COUNT` are trivially invertible (`+x` on insert, `-x` on delete). `AVG` is maintained by storing `(sum, count)` and dividing at read time. `MIN`/`MAX` handle inserts in `O(1)` but require a secondary index or heap if the current extremum is deleted.
- **Holistic Aggregates (`MEDIAN`, `PERCENTILE_CONT`, `COUNT(DISTINCT)`)**: Cannot be updated from a scalar delta alone; engines use sketches like **HyperLogLog** (`uniqHLL12`) or **t-digest** (`quantileTDigestState`) to stay incremental.

## Comparing refresh strategies across engines

| Strategy | Engine Example | Read Blocking | Compute Cost | Freshness | Best Fit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Full Exclusive Refresh** | Postgres `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW` | Yes (`AccessExclusiveLock`) | `O(N)` full scan | Minutes–Hours | Off-peak batch reports |
| **Concurrent Diff Refresh** | Postgres `REFRESH ... CONCURRENTLY` | None (`RowExclusiveLock`) | `O(N)` scan + `O(M)` diff | 5–60 min | Production APIs < 100M rows |
| **Blue/Green Table Swap** | `CREATE TABLE new ...; RENAME` | Brief metadata lock (< 5 ms) | `O(N)` full rebuild | 5–60 min | High-churn tables where diff is slow |
| **Ingest-Time Incremental MV** | ClickHouse `AggregatingMergeTree` | None | `O(Δ)` per insert block | Sub-second–5 s | Append-only event/telemetry streams |
| **Log / Dynamic Table IVM** | Snowflake Dynamic Tables / Flink CDC | None | `O(Δ)` micro-batch | 10 s–5 min | Multi-stage DAGs with SLA lag |

## Failure modes

1. **Non-Concurrent Lock Pileup**: A 4-minute exclusive refresh blocks all incoming API `SELECT`s, exhausting the app's connection pool in 5 seconds. *Mitigation*: Require `CONCURRENTLY` (with a unique index) or atomic table swaps in CI linting.
2. **Refresh Interval Overrun**: Table growth pushes refresh time past the cron period, causing two refreshes to collide and thrash I/O. *Mitigation*: Guard jobs with advisory locks (`pg_try_advisory_lock`) and migrate to incremental/partitioned rollups before utilization hits 70%.
3. **Source `DELETE`/`UPDATE` Drift in Append-Only MVs**: ClickHouse MVs only fire on `INSERT`; an `ALTER TABLE ... DELETE` on the source leaves stale totals in the target MV. *Mitigation*: Use `ReplacingMergeTree` with versioned upserts or explicit partition-level recomputation.
4. **Autovacuum & Temp-Disk Exhaustion**: Frequent `CONCURRENTLY` refreshes generate dead tuples and large temp sort files. *Mitigation*: Tune `autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor` on the MV and size `work_mem` / temp storage.

## Partitioned & Lambda-hybrid patterns

When a single MV grows too large for full refresh yet needs exact SQL semantics:

- **Time-Partitioned Rollup Tables**: Freeze historical partitions (e.g., `day < today - 1`) as immutable tables and only refresh the hot `today` + `yesterday` partitions every 5 minutes.
- **Hot/Cold Union View**: Expose a `VIEW` that `UNION ALL`s a precomputed `historical_mv` (up to midnight) with a live indexed query on `events WHERE ts >= today`, giving **zero staleness** while scanning < 0.5% of total data.

## Practical checklist

- [ ] Define the exact staleness SLA (e.g., `< 60 s` vs `15 min`) and verify readers can tolerate it.
- [ ] Add a `UNIQUE` index for `CONCURRENTLY` refreshes plus secondary indexes matching actual `WHERE`/`ORDER BY` clauses.
- [ ] Guard scheduled refreshes with an advisory lock to prevent overlapping runs.
- [ ] Store non-additive metrics as `(sum, count)` or sketch states (`HLL`, `t-digest`) for incremental safety.
- [ ] Monitor `refresh_duration_seconds`, `staleness_seconds`, and dead-tuple bloat with automated alerts.

nodes.label: Refresh / IVM Engine
nodes.role: Temp snapshot diff or CDC delta agg

steps.title: 1. Normal Request Ingress
steps.explanation: Materialized view refresh precomputes and updates expensive joins or aggregations on disk so analytical queries read in milliseconds, trading bounded staleness and write/refresh overhead for read speed.

steps.title: 2. Core Execution & State Lookup
steps.explanation: Materialized View Store applies the primary invariant and coordinates with Dashboard / API Readers.

steps.title: 3. Scale Spike / Failure Injection
steps.explanation: Under a 10x burst, Dashboard / API Readers experiences contention and tail-latency amplification.

steps.title: 4. Mitigation & Steady Recovery
steps.explanation: Always add a `UNIQUE` index and use `CONCURRENTLY`, or build a new table and atomically `ALTER TABLE ... RENAME`.

tipsAndTricks: Core mental model: Choose full concurrent refresh for simple batch dashboards, and incremental or CDC-driven refresh when tables exceed tens of millions of rows or require sub-minute freshness.
Avoid trap: Forgetting to create indexes on the materialized view itself (it starts with zero indexes beyond any required unique index).
Avoid trap: Using `REFRESH ... CONCURRENTLY` on an empty or newly created MV before an initial non-concurrent populate.
When to reach for it: Read-heavy dashboards, leaderboards, and APIs executing repeated multi-table `JOIN` + `GROUP BY` aggregations over millions of rows.
When to reach for it: Systems that can tolerate bounded staleness (e.g., 5 seconds to 1 hour) in exchange for predictable < 20 ms read latency.

putItTogether.title: Putting Materialized View Refresh Together
putItTogether.summary: Choose full concurrent refresh for simple batch dashboards, and incremental or CDC-driven refresh when tables exceed tens of millions of rows or require sub-minute freshness.
steps: Establish baseline invariants for Materialized View Refresh before scaling.
Isolate hot paths with caching, backpressure, or partitioning.
Verify failure modes with synthetic load & chaos checks.
putItTogether.outcome: Creating a daily-rollup MV with a `UNIQUE (tenant_id, day)` index and scheduling `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY` every 15 minutes dropped portal p99 from 14 s to 11 ms with zero read locks.
